# Input

A compound text field with a label, optional hint, prefix icons, suffix icons, prefix labels, and interactive suffix buttons. Built with slots and Context - each part is a named export.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="search">Search</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputPrefix><MagnifyingGlass /></InputPrefix>
    <InputField id="search" placeholder="Search components…" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add input
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/input/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import {
  InputRoot,
  InputField,
  InputLabel,
} from "@/components/ui/input"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
      <InputLabel htmlFor="email">Email</InputLabel>
      <InputRoot>
        <InputField id="email" placeholder="you@example.com" type="email" />
      </InputRoot>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Playground

The props dress the shell; the parts are everything around the field. A label, a hint, a leading icon and a trailing slot are all children you compose, so each one you switch off disappears from the code.

## Label & hint

`InputLabel` sits above the control - wire it to the field with `htmlFor` pointing at the `InputField`’s `id` so clicking the label focuses the input. Pass `required` to append a destructive asterisk. `InputHint` renders helper text below; give it an `id` and reference it from the field’s `aria-describedby`.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="workspace" required>
    Workspace name
  </InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField
      id="workspace"
      placeholder="acme-inc"
      aria-describedby="workspace-hint"
    />
  </InputRoot>
  <InputHint id="workspace-hint">
    Used in your team URL. Lowercase letters and dashes only.
  </InputHint>
</div>
```

## Prefix icon

Use `InputPrefix` to place a decorative icon on the left. The slot sizes any `svg` automatically and marks it `aria-hidden` so it stays invisible to assistive tech.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="email-prefix">Email address</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputPrefix><EnvelopeSimple /></InputPrefix>
    <InputField id="email-prefix" placeholder="you@example.com" type="email" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Suffix icon

Use `InputSuffix` to place a decorative icon on the right - useful for status indicators or type hints.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="search-suffix">Search</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField id="search-suffix" placeholder="Search…" />
    <InputSuffix><MagnifyingGlass /></InputSuffix>
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Prefix label

`InputPrefixLabel` renders a fixed text segment flush against the left border - ideal for URL schemes, currency symbols, or units. It uses a negative margin to reach the container edge and `overflow-hidden` on the root clips it at the rounded corner.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="domain">Custom domain</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputPrefixLabel>https://</InputPrefixLabel>
    <InputField id="domain" placeholder="yourdomain.com" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>

<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="domain-icon">Custom domain</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputPrefixLabel><Globe /></InputPrefixLabel>
    <InputField id="domain-icon" placeholder="yourdomain.com" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Suffix button

`InputSuffixButton` renders an interactive ghost button inside the field - e.g. a clear action. Always pass `aria-label` since there is no visible text.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="clearable">Project name</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField id="clearable" defaultValue="clearable value" />
    <InputSuffixButton aria-label="Clear" onClick={() => {}}>
      <X className="size-4" />
    </InputSuffixButton>
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Password

`PasswordInput` is a convenience wrapper that manages the show/hide toggle internally. It renders `InputRoot` + `InputField` + `InputSuffixButton` with an Eye / EyeSlash icon from Phosphor. Pass `rootClassName` to style the wrapper, and all other props go to the underlying `input` element.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="password">Password</InputLabel>
  <PasswordInput id="password" placeholder="Enter your password" />
</div>
```

## Number

`NumberInput` adds stepper controls that clamp to `min`/`max`, snap to `step`, and respond to `↑`/`↓` keys, click, and press-and-hold to repeat. The default `stacked` carets sit on the right; `layout="inline"` gives a `−` / `+` quantity stepper with full-height hit targets.

```tsx
// stacked (default)
<NumberInput value={value} onValueChange={setValue} min={0} max={100} />

// inline quantity stepper
<NumberInput layout="inline" value={qty} onValueChange={setQty} min={1} max={10} />
```

## Quantity stepper

The `layout="inline"` `NumberInput` **is** the `−` value `+` quantity stepper: compact, clamped at `min`, and keyboard- and hold-to-repeat friendly. It's the control behind a cart row's [`OrderSummaryItemQuantity`](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/order-summary.md) (see Order Summary → Shopping cart). Give it a fixed `rootClassName` width so it stays tidy in a row.

```tsx
<NumberInput
  layout="inline"
  size="sm"
  value={qty}
  onValueChange={setQty}
  min={1}
  max={99}
  rootClassName="w-24"
  aria-label="Quantity"
/>
```

## Phone

`PhoneInput` pairs the field with a searchable country picker - circular flags, type-to-filter, full keyboard navigation, and a live `+code` prefix. `onChange` reports a `{ country, dialCode, nationalNumber, e164 }` payload; store `e164` as the canonical value. The country segment takes the field's resolved size, so inside a `Form` it grows with the other controls and its hover fills flush to the border.

```tsx
<PhoneInput
  defaultCountry="US"
  defaultValue="555 0142"
  onChange={(p) => console.log(p.e164)}
/>
```

## Sizes

Three sizes on a 4px grid - `sm` (32 px), `md` (36 px, the default), and `lg` (40 px). Set `size` on `InputRoot`; all parts pick it up from context.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="size-sm">Small</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot size="sm">
    <InputField id="size-sm" placeholder="Small" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>

<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="size-md">Medium (default)</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot size="md">
    <InputField id="size-md" placeholder="Medium" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>

<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="size-lg">Large</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot size="lg">
    <InputField id="size-lg" placeholder="Large" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Error

Pass `hasError` to `InputRoot` to switch the border and focus ring to the destructive color and set `aria-invalid` on the underlying `input`. Pass the same `hasError` to `InputHint` so the helper text doubles as the error message.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="email-error" required>Email</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot hasError>
    <InputField
      id="email-error"
      defaultValue="wrong@"
      type="email"
      aria-describedby="email-error-hint"
    />
  </InputRoot>
  <InputHint id="email-error-hint" hasError>
    Enter a valid email address.
  </InputHint>
</div>
```

## Disabled

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="disabled">Email</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot disabled>
    <InputField id="disabled" placeholder="Disabled" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## Inline

Pass `variant="inline"` to `InputRoot` for a chromeless field: the border and fill stay invisible at rest and the container only materializes on hover, while focus keeps the usual brand ring. Perfect for edit-in-place UI - editable titles, table cells, or settings rows that should read as plain text until you reach for them.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
  <InputLabel htmlFor="inline-title">Project title</InputLabel>
  <InputRoot variant="inline">
    <InputField id="inline-title" defaultValue="Untitled project" />
  </InputRoot>
</div>
```

## FAQ

### Why is the input split into InputRoot and InputField?

`InputRoot` is the bordered container that owns the size, error, and disabled state and shares it via context, while `InputField` is the actual `<input>`. Splitting them lets `InputPrefix`, `InputSuffix`, and buttons sit inside the same border as siblings of the field.

### Where do I set the size, and does it propagate to the parts?

Set `size` on `InputRoot` (`sm`, `md`, the default, or `lg`). Every part reads it from context, so the prefix, suffix, and field all scale together.

### When should I use InputSuffix versus InputSuffixButton?

Use `InputSuffix` for a decorative, non-interactive icon (it is marked `aria-hidden`). Use `InputSuffixButton` for an interactive control like a clear action, and always pass `aria-label` since it has no visible text.

### How do I show a validation error?

Pass `hasError` to `InputRoot` to switch the border and focus ring to the destructive color and set `aria-invalid` on the input. Pass the same `hasError` to `InputHint` so the helper text reads as the error message.

### Should I build my own password show/hide toggle?

No. Use `PasswordInput`, which wraps `InputRoot` + `InputField` + `InputSuffixButton` and manages the Eye / EyeSlash toggle internally. Use `rootClassName` to style the wrapper; other props pass through to the input.

### What value should I store from PhoneInput?

Store `e164` as the canonical value. `onChange` reports a `{ country, dialCode, nationalNumber, e164 }` payload, and `e164` is the normalized form you can persist and re-parse.

### Why does the text grow to 16px on a phone?

On a touch screen, `sm` and `md` fields switch from 14px to 16px text (`pointer-coarse:text-base`). iOS zooms the whole page into any focused field under 16px, and it decides by input device rather than screen width, so the rule keys on the pointer too: a desktop keeps 14px at any width. Textarea, PromptInput, the compact Command search, and the Select, MultiSelect, DatePicker and CountrySelect triggers that sit beside a field do the same.

### What happens when the browser autofills the field?

The frame takes a 6% brand tint over whatever surface it sits on, and the text keeps the theme's foreground color. Without it, Chrome and Safari paint their own yellow or blue and force near-black text, which is unreadable in the dark themes. It comes from the `autofill-tint` and `autofill-clear` utilities in globals.css, already applied to `InputRoot` and `InputField`.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add input` writes `components/ui/input/`. Import from `@/components/ui/input`:

- Components and helpers: `InputRoot`, `InputField`, `InputLabel`, `InputHint`, `InputPrefix`, `InputSuffix`, `InputPrefixLabel`, `InputSuffixButton`, `PasswordInput`, `inputVariants`, `NumberInput`, `PhoneInput`, `CountrySelect`, `COUNTRIES`, `COUNTRY_BY_ISO2`
- Types: `InputRootProps`, `InputFieldProps`, `InputLabelProps`, `InputHintProps`, `InputPrefixProps`, `InputSuffixProps`, `InputPrefixLabelProps`, `InputSuffixButtonProps`, `PasswordInputProps`, `NumberInputProps`, `PhoneInputProps`, `PhoneChangePayload`, `CountrySelectProps`, `Country`
- Koala components it installs with it: `label`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `density`, `field-context`, `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`, `country-flag-icons`, `radix-ui`
